create.name: William Cooper
create.bio:
William Cooper is an American meditation teacher whose subject is awakening: recognising, by direct experience, the aware self that is untouched by passing thoughts and moods. He studied psychology and studio art at Vanderbilt and Florida State, completed a four-year Master of Theology at Harding seminary in Memphis in 1982, and later qualified as a counsellor. He has meditated since 1973, served as board president of a Unity church, trained in the Oneness movement, and since 2004 has made many long stays in India and Bhutan, often near the hill of Arunachala at Tiruvannamalai.

His approach blends Eastern teaching with a practical Western eye. The core practice he gives is simple: sit, rest the gaze forward, and let whatever arises unwind without getting involved, ideally for an hour a day. He supports this with short written contemplations, longer story-based writings first shared with a group he led in Austin, Texas, and a free podcast of well over a hundred short episodes meant to be heard in order. He now holds free live sessions every few weeks, open to anyone who wants to listen or ask questions, and is clear that these awakening groups are separate from his work as a therapist.

free_resources.title: William Cooper on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: His numbered series of short talks on awakening and meditation, along with brief guided sits, free to hear in the app or on the web. He also announces his free live question-and-answer sessions here.

free_resources.title: Awakening Together, Relaxing into Happiness (podcast)
free_resources.description: A free podcast of short episodes, each on one aspect of awakening or meditation. William suggests starting at episode one, since each builds on the last, though any can be heard alone.

free_resources.title: Awakening Meditation
free_resources.description: Written instructions for the one practice he teaches most: sitting with eyes closed, resting as plain awareness and letting thoughts and feelings settle without engaging them. He explains how long to sit and what to do when you get caught up.

free_resources.title: Contemplations
free_resources.description: A growing set of short numbered reflections, each opening with a small story and ending with a question to sit with for a few days. Together they point at the difference between who we are and the thoughts we hold about ourselves.

free_resources.title: Writings
free_resources.description: Longer essays drawn from his own experiences, first sent to members of a group he led in Austin. They can be read in any order and lean on true stories to make the teaching concrete.

sprint.tier_evidence: Insight Timer 4k (profile via WebFetch, 1 Nov 2026); no YouTube, Instagram, Facebook or X accounts found on his site or profile; podcast audience figures not counted → ~4k total → local_hero
flags: Owner check (health rule): he is a Licensed Professional Counselor in private practice. His site says the awakening groups, podcasts and writings are not psychotherapy and sells nothing; the only health-adjacent content is a resources page that recommends other people's material, including a PTSD video. Plan written; owner to confirm.

Availability set to worldwide: the meetings page says his group now meets only through free live sessions on Insight Timer. Insight Timer gives Tallahassee, Florida as his location, and the contact page's phone number is an Austin, Texas number, but no current in-person meetings are listed.
Only one photo could be confirmed (his Insight Timer profile picture, 640 px); his site has no photo of him.
No paid offerings, videos or books: the page rests on five free resources (Insight Timer plus four on his own site and podcast).
Listing name drops 'M.Th., Licensed Professional Counselor' from his Insight Timer display name.
left_out: Resources page (links to Mooji, Ram Dass and others, plus a PTSD video): other people's material and a condition-named item.
Phone number on the contact page: not needed for the listing.
Older in-person meetings in Austin: no longer running according to the meetings page.
